$comment: HAND-AUTHORED overlay model rows — the reviewed half of the catalog, which upstream extraction and live discovery may never overwrite (WS-13 §7). One resolvable row per cohort provider (two or three where a lane needs a plain, a reasoning and a flagship model), so every adapter lane has something to resolve against its loopback fake. EVERY row is `status: "candidate"`: promotion to `supported` requires the behavioural corpus (WS-13 §13), which no row has run. NO row carries `classifierEligible` — R6-14 sets that only after the safety corpus passes live, so the answer here is Manual fallback, the fail-safe direction. `pricing` is present ONLY where a vendor's own pricing page states a list price for that exact model, with the page URL as `sourceRef` and the observation instant: R6-H makes this the only price source and `costBasis: "list"` a claim about published prices, so an unpriced row carries no `pricing` key at all rather than an invented number. Gateway, Azure-deployment, Bedrock and Vertex rows are deliberately unpriced — their prices are the reseller's, not the vendor list, and no page was read for them.

models.$comment: Upstream's own static fallback rows — the live roster changes as volunteer workers come and go, so `modelDiscovery` is the real catalogue and these are a seed. `toolCalling` is `none` as a FACT here, not a fail-closed default: the backends do not implement it, and `unsupportedParameters` carries the three fields that 500 if sent.

models.$comment: Standard paid tier <=200k prompt tokens; >200k $2.50/$15/$0.25. Gemini 2.5 access is limited to users who actively used these models in the past; Google explicitly says they are not deprecated and will be served until further notice (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models). Native reasoning uses thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget (not thinkingLevel); 2.5 Pro cannot disable thinking; Flash/Flash-Lite can set budget 0 (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thinking). Google documents thought signatures for Gemini 3 and 2.5; preserve original parts across tool turns (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thinking).

summaryRequest.sourceRef: continuity report §6.1 — `config.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts: true` on generateContent. The field is a BOOLEAN, recorded here as its single enabling spelling because the schema's `values` is a string list; the Interactions API's `generation_config.thinking_summaries` is a different surface and is not claimed for this endpoint.

continuationDomain.sourceRef: continuity report §6.1, BOTH halves. Own-state acceptance: a `thoughtSignature` is returned to the SAME model on its exact original part — "do not concatenate signed parts; do not move a signature to a different part; preserve every accumulated signature in a sequential function-call turn". Why the domain is NARROW: "A Gemini summary can be forwarded to another family. The `thoughtSignature` cannot." Signatures are bound to their exact part and model, so the domain is this model alone.

pricing.sourceRef: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing — Gemini 2.5 Pro paid tier, prompts <= 200k tokens: input $1.25, output $10.00, context-cache read $0.125 per 1M tokens. TIERED UPSTREAM: prompts > 200k are billed $2.50 / $15.00 / $0.25. `ModelPricing` has one rate per direction, so the STANDARD (<=200k) tier is recorded and cost is UNDER-reported for prompts above it — a disclosed schema gap (PROVENANCE.md), not a claim that the higher tier does not exist.

models.$comment: R6b-5: duplicated from the `zai-anthropic` sibling's upstream facts with its own key. `toolCalling` fails CLOSED because upstream states no flag for these rows — see WS-13 §8.1. Reasoning evidence added for SDK 0.0.11 (R-10b-8/W18-16, router review findings): GLM exposes readable `reasoning_content` (full-exposed, like DeepSeek), so this row must never be treated as a model with nothing to lose, and its own carriage (as a SOURCE, cross-family) must render `kind="exposed"`, not `kind="summary"`. `continuation` is `plaintext`: Z.ai's own Preserved Thinking / Interleaved Thinking docs (docs.z.ai/guides/capabilities/thinking-mode, and `ChatThinking.clear_thinking` on docs.z.ai/api-reference/llm/chat-completion) document forwarding the full historical `reasoning_content` back in `messages` verbatim and in order — the textual passback contract the schema's `plaintext` value exists for, exactly as `deepseek/deepseek-reasoner` already carries. This ALSO fixes same-domain carriage: `capabilitiesFrom`'s `readableState` gates the OpenAI chat-completions adapter's own `captureExposedReasoning` flag (`chat-completions.ts`), which — with `reasoning: null` — was silently disabling GLM's own tool-loop reasoning replay, contrary to Z.ai's default-on Interleaved Thinking. Passback is opt-in (`clear_thinking` defaults `true` = cleared on the standard API endpoint; the Coding Plan endpoint defaults it `false`) — this row states what the documented contract IS once engaged, not that Winter enables it by default. `toolLoopRequirement` is `silent-degradation`, not DeepSeek's `hard-error`: Z.ai's own wording is “may degrade performance ... or prevent the feature from taking effect”, never a stated error response; nothing in this codebase reads `toolLoopRequirement` for behavior today, so this is evidentiary only. No `zai-anthropic/*` sibling gets this: no official Z.ai documentation of an Anthropic-dialect (`/v1/messages`) thinking contract was found (docs.z.ai's own site index carries no such page as of 2026-09-14) — WS-13 §8.2 forbids assuming one dialect's contract on another, so those rows stay untouched.

P7a upgrade: this row previously cited the MODELS page, which states input/output and the cache-read multiplier but no cache-write rate (P6.6 could not reach the pricing page). `cacheWritePerMTokUsd` records the 5-MINUTE write ($12.50), matching every other Anthropic row here; the 1-hour write ($20) has no field of its own and is under-reported, exactly as `ModelPricing`'s one-rate-per-direction shape requires — a disclosed schema gap, not a claim the 1h rate does not exist. Batch (-50%), fast-mode and `inference_geo: "us"` (1.1x) modifiers are likewise unrepresentable and are NOT folded into these numbers.

completionEvent.sourceRef: R6-D's pinned stream vocabulary — a thinking block's `signature` arrives across `signature_delta` events, so the COMPLETE replayable block exists only at `content_block_stop`

continuationDomain.sourceRef: continuity report §4.4, BOTH halves. Own-state acceptance: §4.4 requires the model's own assistant blocks — `thinking` with its signature, `redacted_thinking` — replayed unchanged and in order across a tool loop. Why the domain is NARROW: Anthropic documents model switching as a boundary at which those blocks are STRIPPED, because they are tied to the producing model; "same provider" is therefore not "same continuation domain", and this domain is the model alone.

models.$comment: Model and aliases documented at https://docs.x.ai/developers/models/grok-4.7. The catalog's xai provider currently declares Chat Completions; xAI also offers Responses.  No model-specific max output token cap was found. xAI's models page says logprobs/top_logprobs on grok-4.20 and newer are silently ignored, not rejected (https://docs.x.ai/developers/models). Legacy Anthropic-compatible POST /v1/messages remains documented but fully deprecated (https://docs.x.ai/developers/rest-api-reference/inference/legacy); unauthenticated POST today returned 401 after validating the request, so route exists but successful inference was not verified. POST /anthropic returned 404. https://docs.x.ai/developers/model-capabilities/text/reasoning says presencePenalty, frequencyPenalty, and stop return an error on reasoning models (snake_case names recorded for the Chat Completions wire). Chat Completions does not carry encrypted reasoning ciphertext; Grok 4.7 Responses does, so continuation is 'none' for this chat provider.

models.$comment: No pricing: this is a subscription credential, not public API per-token billing. https://github.com/kenryu42/pi-grok-cli lists grok-4.7 on an unofficial OAuth client; https://github.com/stnly/pi-grok documents cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1, account-dependent live /v1/models enrichment, and Responses requests. https://github.com/kenryu42/pi-grok-cli lists 500K registered context but cautions this may differ from enforced limits. Current Winter xai-oauth provider descriptor claims openai-chat-completions, in conflict with the available community integration evidence for Responses; do not assume chat compatibility without a live test. No proxy-specific aliases, max output, parallel tools, structured output, caching, exact effort values, or reasoning continuation contract found. Availability depends on subscription/account tier and rollout.
